hints: Identify the force acting on a surface and the area over which that force is distributed.
walkthrough: Pressure describes how much normal force acts on each unit area of a surface.
Therefore, pressure is normal force divided by area.

ai_rubric.observable: States that pressure is normal force per unit area.

hints: Use the pressure definition from (a)(i), then express both force and area using SI base units.
Replace force with kg m s⁻² and area with m² before simplifying the quotient.
walkthrough: From the definition, p = F / A.
Force has SI base units kg m s⁻² and area has SI base units m².
Therefore [p] = (kg m s⁻²) / m² = kg m⁻¹ s⁻².

ai_rubric.observable: Uses p = F / A with force in kg m s⁻² and area in m² to obtain kg m⁻¹ s⁻².

hints: Make k the subject of the supplied equation, then replace each quantity by its SI base units.
Use [p] = kg m⁻¹ s⁻², [R] = [L] = m, [ρ] = kg m⁻³, [t] = s and [m] = kg; numerical constants have no units.
walkthrough: Rearrange the supplied equation: k = π(p₂ − p₁)R⁴ρt / (8Lm). The factors π and 8 have no units.
Use [p₂ − p₁] = kg m⁻¹ s⁻², [R] = m, [ρ] = kg m⁻³, [t] = s, [L] = m and [m] = kg.
Cancelling the powers gives [k] = kg m⁻¹ s⁻¹.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses metres for R and L and seconds for t.
Uses density in kg m⁻³, or derives that unit from mass divided by volume.
Substitutes the base units into the rearranged equation and simplifies the units of k to kg m⁻¹ s⁻¹.

hints: For a quantity raised to a power, its percentage uncertainty contribution is multiplied by that power.
Compare the contribution from R⁴ with the contribution from L, using the 2% uncertainty given for each measurement.
walkthrough: From the rearranged equation, k is proportional to R⁴ and inversely proportional to L.
The exponent 4 makes the percentage uncertainty contribution from R equal to 4 × 2% = 8%.
The contribution from L is 2%, since its power is one.
Therefore, R contributes more to the percentage uncertainty in k.

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies R as the larger contribution because R⁴ gives 8% from a 2% uncertainty, whereas L gives 2%.
